title: How JavaScript runs — quick overview
rememberThis: JavaScript runs on an engine (V8), not the CLR — dynamic types at run time; TypeScript erases; C# keeps IL metadata.
V8: parse → Ignition bytecode → TurboFan for hot paths → deopt on type/shape change. Warm up before benchmarking.
Call stack (who runs) ≠ scope chain (lexical lookup). Closures keep outer environments on the heap.
Event loop: sync → all microtasks (promises) → one macrotask (timers). setTimeout(0) is not instant.
ES modules are always strict with module scope; classic scripts allow sloppy mode and global var.
bullets: Three layers: ECMAScript language, engine (V8), host (browser or Node.js) — not dotnet IL.
Hoisting: var → undefined; let/const → temporal dead zone; function declarations hoist fully.
Strict mode: no implicit globals, undefined this in plain functions — on by default in modules.
async/await schedules microtasks — does not create OS threads; CPU work blocks the loop.
import evaluates modules; C# using only aliases names. Node: CJS require vs ESM import.
